about: The closed roster of classical commentators, per plan. A teaching's sentence names, after its semicolon, one of the display names allowed for its plan (two where schools differ), and the gate fails any name not listed or any day outside the commentator's coverage. Coverage lists book names exactly as the plan's labels print them; "all" covers the whole plan. A source may be opened by a verifier; the evidence quotes the commentator's own words from a source actually opened, at most 40 words from any copyrighted English. Rule of thumb: published before 1931 is public domain in the United States in 2026.

bible.note: The shared Fathers: venerated in both the Catholic and Orthodox traditions and read by Protestants as early church writers. Not on the roster: Origen and Tertullian (contested), Clement of Alexandria, and the Catena Aurea’s later and anonymous voices (Theophylact, Remigius, Rabanus, Alcuin, Haymo, the Gloss, “Greek Ex.”, Pseudo-Chrysostom and the other pseudonymous extracts).

wang-bi.name: Wang Bi
sources: Chinese text on zh.wikisource.org or ctext.org (public domain)
Legge's notes, SBE 39 (1891), as a conduit
traps: Wang Bi's base text differs from Legge's in places: confirm the line he comments on is the line in the day's chapter.
Name him plainly: no title.

heshang-gong.name: the Heshang Gong commentary
heshang-gong.dates: Han dynasty or later; its author is unknown
sources: Chinese text on zh.wikisource.org or ctext.org (public domain)
Legge's notes, SBE 39 (1891), which translate its chapter titles
traps: The name is a legend (the Old Man by the River): name the commentary, never tell his story or treat him as a historical author.
Its chapter titles (for example ‘Embodying the Tao’ for chapter 1) are part of the commentary and may be cited as its reading.

guo-xiang.name: Guo Xiang
sources: Chinese text on ctext.org or zh.wikisource.org (public domain)
Legge, SBE 39 and 40 (1891), as a conduit
traps: Guo Xiang's commentary covers the 33-chapter recension, which Giles follows; locate by opening words, not paragraph number.
Giles' own notes are printed in the app's text and are not a key verse and not Guo Xiang.

zhu-xi.name: Zhu Xi
zhu-xi.work: Collected Commentaries on the Analects (Lunyu jizhu)
sources: Chinese text on ctext.org (public domain)
Legge's notes, The Chinese Classics vol. 1 (1893), as a conduit
traps: Zhu Xi's chapter divisions differ from Legge's in places: locate by opening words.

he-yan.name: He Yan
he-yan.work: Collected Explanations of the Analects (Lunyu jijie)
sources: Chinese text on ctext.org (public domain)
traps: The Jijie gathers earlier glosses under their authors' names (Kong Anguo, Ma Rong, Zheng Xuan): say ‘He Yan's collected commentary’ or name the gathered author as given there.

dhp-commentary.name: the Theravāda commentary
dhp-commentary.dates: fifth century, ascribed by tradition to Buddhaghosa
sources: The Pali text: Chaṭṭha Saṅgāyana, Vipassana Research Institute, s0502a.att.xml (free for non-commercial use, with attribution): the explanation of every verse

E. W. Burlingame, Buddhist Legends, Harvard Oriental Series 28 to 30 (1921), archive.org buddhistlegends01budd to 03budd (public domain): the stories, which frame each verse; Burlingame omits the word-by-word explanations except on verses 324, 354 and 415
Max Müller’s notes, SBE 10 (1881), as a conduit
traps: Never state the ascription to Buddhaghosa as fact.

The reading is the lesson the commentary draws from the verse: from its Pali explanation (Tattha ...), or from the story as Burlingame translates it, located by book and story (Burlingame I.4) and the Norman page he prints.
Burlingame leaves out the verse explanations (except 324, 354, 415): a reading of a word in the verse comes from the Pali, with the verifier’s gloss.
Some stories only point to another (“the same as the foregoing”): read the story they point to.

shankara.name: Śaṅkara
shankara.work: Bhāṣya (commentary) on the Gita and on the Upanishads
sources: Gita: A. Mahadeva Sastri, The Bhagavad-Gita with the Commentary of Sri Sankaracharya (1897; 2nd ed. 1901), archive.org (public domain)
Isa and Kena: S. Sitarama Sastri, The Upanishads and Sri Sankara's Commentary vol. 1 (1898); Katha: vol. 2 (1898), archive.org (public domain)
traps: Name the school (Advaita) whenever a second commentator is named.

ramanuja.name: Rāmānuja
sources: Gita: A. Govindacharya, Sri Bhagavad-Gita with Sri Ramanujacharya's Visishtadvaita Commentary (1898), archive.org (public domain)
Upanishads: only where the Śrī Bhāṣya treats the verse, G. Thibaut, SBE 48 (1904) (public domain)
traps: He wrote no commentary on the Isa, Kena or Katha: on an Upanishad day name him only where the Śrī Bhāṣya treats the verse, and name the Śrī Bhāṣya as the place.
Always name his school (Viśiṣṭādvaita).

madhva.name: Madhva
sources: Gita: S. Subba Rau, The Bhagavad-Gita, translated with the commentary of Sri Madhwacharya (1906), archive.org (public domain)
Isa, Kena, Katha: S. C. Vasu, The Sacred Books of the Hindus vol. 1 (1909 to 1911), archive.org (public domain)
traps: Always name his school (Dvaita).

sayana.name: Sāyaṇa
sources: H. H. Wilson, Rig-Veda-Sanhita, 6 vols (1850 to 1888), which follows Sāyaṇa, archive.org (public domain)
Max Müller's edition of the Rig Veda with Sāyaṇa's commentary (1849 to 1874), for the Sanskrit
traps: Wilson numbers by aṣṭaka and adhyāya as well: store and cite mandala.hymn.verse.
When the reading is known only through Wilson, use the ‘as given in’ source form.

yaska.name: Yāska
sources: Lakshman Sarup, The Nighantu and the Nirukta (1920 to 1921), archive.org (public domain)
traps: Yāska treats only some verses: name him only where the Nirukta treats the verse, with the Nirukta's book and section.

tabari.name: al-Tabari
sources: quran.com API, tafsir id 15 (Arabic), by ayah
traps: Paraphrase only.
Al-Tabari reports several readings with their chains: say which one he prefers only where he says so.

ibn-kathir.name: Ibn Kathir
sources: quran.com API, tafsir id 14 (Arabic), by ayah
tafsir id 169 is the abridged English (Darussalam, copyrighted): at most 40 words, and find the reading in the Arabic
traps: The English ‘Ibn Kathir’ is an abridgement: find the reading in the Arabic.

jalalayn.name: the Jalalayn
sources: altafsir.com, one ayah at a time (the English by Feras Hamza is copyrighted by the Royal Aal al-Bayt Institute: fair dealing only, never bulk)
traps: Two authors: al-Mahalli wrote on al-Fatiha and surahs 18 to 114, al-Suyuti on 2 to 17. Say ‘the Jalalayn’ or the right author.

qurtubi.name: al-Qurtubi
sources: quran.com API, tafsir id 90 (Arabic), by ayah
traps: Paraphrase only.

wahidi.name: al-Wahidi
sources: Asbab al-Nuzul in Arabic; name the report as he gives it
traps: He treats only some ayahs: name him only where he gives an occasion for the ayah.

tabarsi.name: the Shi’i commentator al-Tabarsi
sources: Majmaʿ al-bayān in Arabic
traps: Named only where the Shi’i reading differs materially, and then beside a Sunni commentator, the difference named and not resolved.

rashi.name: Rashi
rashi.work: Commentary on the Torah, Prophets and Writings
sources: Sefaria API v3 (https://www.sefaria.org/api/v3/texts/Rashi_on_Genesis.22.8): Torah in English by Rosenbaum and Silbermann (1929 to 1934, public domain) and Metsudah (2009, CC-BY); Prophets and Writings by the Judaica Press, trans. A. J. Rosenberg (CC-BY)
traps: The commentary on Chronicles printed under his name is widely held not to be his: not covered.
For Ezra and Nehemiah check Sefaria's notes on the attribution.
Hebrew is the primary evidence; name the English version quoted.

ibn-ezra.name: Ibn Ezra
ibn-ezra.work: Commentaries on the Torah and the Prophets and Writings
sources: Sefaria API v3; the Torah English by Strickman and Silver is CC-BY-NC: evidence only, at most 40 words
traps: The Proverbs commentary under his name is disputed: not covered.

radak.name: Radak
radak.work: Commentaries on Genesis, the Prophets, Psalms and Chronicles
sources: Sefaria API v3

ramban.name: Ramban
sources: Sefaria API v3

rashbam.name: Rashbam
sources: Sefaria API v3
traps: His commentary on the opening chapters of Genesis survives only in part.

sforno.name: Sforno
sforno.work: Commentaries on the Torah and some Writings and Prophets
sources: Sefaria API v3

metzudat-david.name: Metzudat David
metzudat-david.work: Commentary on the Prophets and Writings
sources: Sefaria API v3

midrash.name: the Midrash
midrash.dates: late antiquity to the Middle Ages
midrash.work: the classical Midrash collections, named as a work
sources: Sefaria API v3
traps: Name the collection and its section (‘Genesis Rabbah 56’), never ‘the rabbis say’.

augustine.name: Augustine
augustine.work: Expositions on the Psalms, Tractates on John, City of God, Confessions, sermons
sources: NPNF series 1 (Schaff, 1886 to 1890), ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)
traps: He numbers the Psalms as the Greek and Latin Bibles do: his Psalm 22 is the WEB's 23.
Reading the Latin, he may comment on wording the WEB lacks: choose another verse or say ‘reading the Latin’.

chrysostom.name: John Chrysostom
chrysostom.work: Homilies on Genesis, Matthew, John, Acts and the Pauline letters
sources: NPNF series 1 vols 9 to 14, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)
traps: The Catena's ‘Pseudo-Chrys.’ is the Opus imperfectum, not Chrysostom.

jerome.name: Jerome
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 6, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

gregory-great.name: Gregory the Great
gregory-great.work: Moralia on Job; homilies on the Gospels and Ezekiel
sources: Morals on the Book of Job (Oxford, 1844 to 1850), archive.org (public domain)

basil.name: Basil of Caesarea
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 8, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

ambrose.name: Ambrose
ambrose.work: On the Duties of the Clergy, letters, exegetical works
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 10, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)
traps: Ambrosiaster is not Ambrose.

cyril-alexandria.name: Cyril of Alexandria
cyril-alexandria.work: Commentary on John; Commentary on Luke
sources: Commentary on John (Pusey and Randell, 1874 to 1885) and on Luke (Payne Smith, 1859), ccel.org and archive.org (public domain)

athanasius.name: Athanasius
athanasius.work: On the Incarnation, Against the Arians, letters
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 4, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

irenaeus.name: Irenaeus
sources: ANF vol. 1, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

ephrem.name: Ephrem the Syrian
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 13, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

leo-great.name: Leo the Great
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 12, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

hilary.name: Hilary of Poitiers
hilary.work: On the Trinity; homilies on the Psalms
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 9, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

gregory-nyssa.name: Gregory of Nyssa
gregory-nyssa.work: On the Making of Man; Life of Moses; homilies
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 5, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

gregory-nazianzus.name: Gregory of Nazianzus
sources: NPNF series 2 vol. 7, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

cyprian.name: Cyprian
sources: ANF vol. 5, ccel.org and newadvent.org/fathers (public domain)

bede.name: Bede
bede.work: Commentaries on Mark, Luke and Acts; homilies
sources: as gathered in the Catena Aurea (Newman, 1841 to 1845), ccel.org (public domain)

matthew-henry.name: the Protestant commentator Matthew Henry
matthew-henry.work: Exposition of the Old and New Testaments
sources: ccel.org mhc1 to mhc6 (public domain)
traps: A labelled fallback only: used where no Father on the day's chapters is found, at most one day in ten, and only Genesis to Acts (Romans to Revelation were finished by others).

hippolytus.name: Hippolytus
hippolytus.work: Scholia on Daniel; On Christ and Antichrist
sources: ANF vol. 5 (1886), ccel.org (public domain)

victorinus.name: Victorinus of Pettau
sources: ANF vol. 7 (1886), ccel.org (public domain)
traps: His commentary covers 20 of Revelation’s 22 chapters.

gregory-thaumaturgus.name: Gregory Thaumaturgus
sources: ANF vol. 6 (1886), ccel.org (public domain)
traps: A paraphrase of the whole book: a reading from it is his rendering of the line, located by chapter.

legge-sbe39.name: Legge's notes
legge-sbe39.full: James Legge, The Texts of Taoism, Sacred Books of the East 39 and 40 (1891)

giles-1889.name: Giles' notes
giles-1889.full: Herbert A. Giles, Chuang Tzu: Mystic, Moralist, and Social Reformer (1889)

legge-cc1.name: Legge's notes
legge-cc1.full: James Legge, The Chinese Classics vol. 1 (2nd ed. 1893)

muller-sbe10.name: Müller's notes
muller-sbe10.full: F. Max Müller, The Dhammapada, Sacred Books of the East 10 (1881)

telang-sbe8.name: Telang's translation
telang-sbe8.full: K. T. Telang, The Bhagavadgita, Sacred Books of the East 8 (1882)
telang-sbe8.use: the verification translation for every Gita key verse, never a commentator

muller-sbe1-15.name: Müller's notes
muller-sbe1-15.full: F. Max Müller, The Upanishads, Sacred Books of the East 1 and 15 (1879, 1884)

griffith-notes.name: Griffith's notes
griffith-notes.full: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889 to 1892)

muller-rv.name: Müller's edition
muller-rv.full: F. Max Müller, Rig-Veda-Sanhita with the commentary of Sayanacharya (1849 to 1874)

catena-aurea.name: the Catena Aurea
catena-aurea.full: Thomas Aquinas, Catena Aurea, trans. J. H. Newman and others (1841 to 1845)
catena-aurea.use: name the Father whose words it gathers, in the form ‘X, as given in the Catena Aurea’
